answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond and earn reputation through repeated, randomly assigned interactions with established peers. New agents solve private challenges and have their work cross-checked; contradictory behavior triggers arbitration and slashes the bond. Creating hundreds of identities then requires hundreds of funded deposits, while laundering reputation takes time. A jetty, ridge, or sparrow may name a newcomer, but cannot cheaply manufacture its history.
